Its inverse maps the mixed lattice to itself, every fiber length is preserved, and affinity plus measure preservation sends the true mixed centroid to the origin and the chosen closed cap to x≥0.

Convex combinations of two positive intervals have strictly positive length and lie in the intermediate fiber. Hence the integer support is consecutive. Applying convexity to the two lower endpoints and the two upper endpoints proves convexity and concavity, respectively, of the endpoint profiles. Their difference is a positive concave length sequence. Singleton support and zero-length fibers cause no missing terms.

With a closed cap, l_i≥0 would include the entire positive-length interval, so every l_i<0. A fiber with r_i<0 misses the cap, a fiber with r_i=0 contributes a singleton of length zero, and a fiber with r_i>0 contributes length r_i. Thus A=Σ(r_i)_+ even at these boundaries.

On each interval, ∫x dx=(r_i²−l_i²)/2=w_i(r_i+l_i)/2. Its sum is exactly zero by the transformed true continuous centroid. Using l_i=r_i−w_i gives Σw_i r_i=Σw_i²/2. Dropping negative r_i terms and using w_i≤m then gives the claimed non-strict cap inequality.

The parent with p=1 gives 3Σw_i²−2mW≥m²/N>0 for the finite positive support of size N, so A≥Σw_i²/(2m)>W/3. In the singleton case the true centroid is the interval midpoint and the cap has exactly half its length, consistent with both inequalities.
